newsDocuments.headline: Iran says no unauthorised vessels transited Strait of Hormuz overnight after navigation aids destroyed

segments.text: DUBAI: Navigational ​aid systems ‌in the south ​of ​the Strait of ⁠Hormuz ​were destroyed ​and no unauthorised vessels ​transited ​the maritime route ‌overnight, ⁠an unnamed Revolutionary Guards ​Navy ​official ⁠told Iranian ​state ​media ⁠

newsDocuments.headline: Oil steadies after Trump signals restraint on Iran, Hormuz risks persist

segments.text: NEW DELHI/PERTH: Oil prices were steady on Monday after US ‌President Donald Trump downplayed the likelihood of new strikes on Iran, though attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz kept supply concerns in focus.
Brent inched up 3 cents to $98.35 a barrel by 0427 GMT, ​while US West Texas Intermediate rose 0.5% to $91.30 a barrel.

Trump said on Sunday ​he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to ​end the conflict progress, even as both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near ‌the Strait ⁠of Hormuz .

newsDocuments.headline: Gold rises over 1% as softer oil prices ease inflation worries

segments.text: Gold rose more than 1% on Monday as softer ‌oil prices eased inflation concerns, while investors awaited key US inflation data and fresh signals from the Federal Reserve on its policy outlook.

Oil prices fell after US President Donald Trump said he ⁠was highly unlikely to order further attacks on Iran as talks to end the conflict ​continued, easing concerns about potential supply disruptions.
Lower oil prices can ease inflationary pressures and ​reduce expectations that interest rates will stay higher for longer, lowering the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.
